messages.content: What's the total number of possible arrangements in a chess game?

function.name: boardgame_calculate_score

message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large.  While the exact count is not known (the space is too huge to enumerate exhaustively), the best estimates put it at roughly

\[
10^{43}\text{–}10^{45}
\]

legal positions.

This estimate comes from combinatorial analyses of the game’s rules and has been refined over decades.  For comparison, the Shannon number for the total number of possible games (sequences of moves) is about \(10^{120}\).  So even just counting the static board configurations already gives us a mind‑blowing figure in the order of tens of trillions of trillions of trillions of trillions of trillions of trillions of trillions of trillions… (i.e., \(10^{43}\)).
